questions_and_answers.question_text: How does Hànyǔ differ from Zhōngwén?

answers.answer_text: Hànyǔ is the more formal term for the Chinese language.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does fùzá mean, and what is its alternate pronunciation?

answers.answer_text: "To be complicated, complex"; also pronounced fùzhá.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the two meanings of xiāngxìn.

answers.answer_text: "To believe in, to have faith in," and "to be convinced, to be certain, to trust that...."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which meaning of xiāngxìn is used in sentence 1B?

answers.answer_text: "To be convinced, to be certain that...."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Translate into English: Wǒ liǎngdiǎn zhōng yǒu Hànyǔ kè.

answers.answer_text: I have Chinese class at two.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Translate into Chinese: That's a complicated question.
Write a Chinese sentence in which xiāngxìn means "to believe in."
Translate into Chinese: I'm certain that he will do a good job.
Translate into Chinese: Don't worry! I'm convinced you can learn it very well.
Explain the difference between speaking Chinese and mastering Hànyǔ as described in this note.

articles.text:
1. A: Hànyǔ hěn fùzá, xuéqilai dàgài hěn nán?!
   Chinese is very complicated. It must be very difficult to study?!
   B: Fàngxīn ba! Wǒ xiāngxìn nǐ kěyi xuéde hěn hǎo.
   Don't worry! I'm convinced you can learn it very well.

Notes on No. 1

Hànyǔ: "Chinese language" This is more formal than Zhōngwén.

Shuō Zhōngguo huà bú tài nán, kěshi yào xuéhǎo Hànyǔ jiù bǐjiào nán le.
It isn't too hard to speak Chinese, but if you want to master the Chinese language, it is more difficult.

Wǒ liǎngdiǎn zhōng yǒu Hànyǔ kè.
I have Chinese class at two.

fùzá: "to be complicated, to be complex" Also pronounced fùzhá.

Nà shi yíge fùzáde wèntí.
That's a complicated question.

xiāngxìn: (1) "to believe in, to have faith in"

Tā xiāngxìn yíge hěn qíguàide zōngjiào.
He believes in a very strange religion.

Wǒ bù xiāngxìn!
I don't believe it!

Yǐqián rénmen bù xiāngxìn zhèizhǒng shuōfǎ, xiànzài xiāngxìn le.
People didn't used to believe in this explanation, but now they do.

(2) (as used in 1B) "to be convinced, to be certain, to trust that..."

Wǒ xiāngxìn tā yídìng zuòde hǎo.
I'm certain that he will do a good job.
